question: According to a statement by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church, at least 60 Christians were killed in two attacks in the Oromia region on 20 and 24 October 2026. Reportedly, more than 20 homes were also set on fire and more than 20 people seriously injured1. These murders highlight the urgent need to protect Christian communities. Specific interventions, accountability and substantive support for those affected are required. In view of the above: 1.
What immediate and concrete actions does the Commission intend to take to protect Christian communities in Ethiopia from new attacks?

Does the Commission intend, in coordination with the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, to promote the consideration of targeted sanctions against those responsible for the murders of Christians, provided that their involvement is documented?

What specific measures, beyond statements of condemnation, does the Commission intend to promote to prevent repeated attacks against Christians in non-EU countries, with a clear timetable for implementation and monitoring of their results?
